title: The approve stage dirties the program worktree, so the first node launch fails "base repository must be clean"
detail: approve() writes prepared subject, gate-evidence, operator-approval and receipt into ROOT/logs/plan-approval/<run_id> (experiments/run_burden_plan_graph.py:333-366). .gitignore ignores only logs/runs/* (.gitignore:7) — verified: `git check-ignore -v logs/plan-approval/run1/receipt.json` exits 1 (not ignored), while logs/runs/x/y.json exits 0. changed_paths() includes untracked files via `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` (harness_labs/git_transaction.py:33-50), and GitWorktreeTransaction.create raises GitTransactionError("base repository must be clean") when changed_paths(base_repository) is non-empty (harness_labs/git_transaction.py:144-145). base_repository is REPO, the program worktree (run_burden_plan_graph.py:74, :651). So the documented sequence decompose -> approve -> run aborts on CB-01's very first worktree creation. Fix is one line (ignore or relocate logs/plan-approval), but as written the program cannot start.
affects: all nodes CB-01..CB-07; the run stage never launches

title: Default run_id is not a legal PlanGraph ID — register_plan_graph raises before any node runs
detail: run_id defaults to datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ') (experiments/run_burden_plan_graph.py:724), feeding logical_graph_id=f'contract-burden-{run_id}' (:680) and graph_run_id=f'cb-graph-{run_id}' (:696-698). register_plan_graph calls validate_plan_graph_id (harness_labs/plan_graph.py:684) and PlanGraph.__init__ calls it again on graph_run_id (harness_labs/plan_graph.py:952); the pattern is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,127}$ (harness_labs/plan_graph_audit.py:43-49). Executed the validator directly: 'contract-burden-20260812T174300Z' and 'cb-graph-20260812T174300Z' both raise "PlanGraph ID must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,127}$" (the uppercase T/Z of the ISO basic timestamp). The run stage therefore fails immediately unless the operator happens to pass a lowercase --run-id; nothing in the plan or runner docstring says it must.
affects: run stage entry point; whole program

title: Every node runs under verification_repair_limit=1 — the exact budget the program cites as the dominant blocker
detail: run_plan_graph_feature_worktree is called without verification_repair_limit (experiments/run_burden_plan_graph.py:646-664), so the default 1 applies (harness_labs/feature_run.py:488). In _verify_with_recovery only 'infrastructure_transient' failures are retried free (harness_labs/feature_run.py:1362-1374, capped at 2); every other classification consumes the single repair and the next failure returns 'blocked' (harness_labs/feature_run.py:1376-1383). classify_verification_failure works from the first 500 chars of stderr+stdout (harness_labs/feature_run.py:404-423) — red_green_check prints only an indented JSON verdict, so a 'red-phase-passed-on-base' verdict (whose red_tail reads like '3 passed in 0.4s') carries no marker and classifies 'indeterminate', still consuming the single repair. A two-phase gate (must FAIL on base, must PASS on candidate) is strictly harder to hit than an ordinary test command, and the plan's own evidence is that 5 of 14 FR-20 attempts died at repair_limit=1 (docs/development/CONTRACT_BURDEN_RELAXATION_PLAN.md:86-90). The program most exposed to this failure mode ships with it unmitigated.

title: Program rule 3 (recover a blocked node via scripts/plan_graph_recover.py) is not wired to this runner
detail: plan_graph_recover resumes by exec'ing `scripts/run_plan_graph.py run --repository ... --registration <path> --graph-attempt-id ... --launcher-command ... --run-root ... --resume` (scripts/plan_graph_recover.py:264-275, :296). Three mechanical gaps: (1) the runner never persists a registration file — persist_registration exists (harness_labs/plan_graph.py:805-830) but run_burden_plan_graph.py only holds the in-memory PlanGraphRegistration (:682-699), so --registration has nothing to point at; (2) node launching is an in-process Python closure (_launch_node, :560-672), not a --launcher-command subprocess, so run_plan_graph.py cannot relaunch a CB node; (3) run_root is per-invocation (ROOT/logs/runs/cb-graph-<run_id>, :696) and RetryBudgetLedger is rooted there (harness_labs/plan_graph.py:982), so a fresh `run` invocation with a new run_id starts a brand-new lineage ledger — the claimed 'live test of the RB retry-budget ledger' does not actually carry state across attempts. Separately, no recovery_agent is passed, so node-level _recover_abnormal returns False immediately (harness_labs/feature_run.py:1161-1162) and every abnormal verification/dispatch condition is terminal.
affects: program rule 3 / recovery-system live-test claim; any blocked node

title: Red-phase attribution is unsound for CB-02..CB-07: the gate only checks that pytest exits non-zero on the frozen base
detail: red_green_check accepts any non-zero red exit as proof (scripts/dev/red_green_check.py:74-84) with RED_BASE frozen at 6fb1fd1 (experiments/run_burden_plan_graph.py:87). Verified 6fb1fd1 vs the graph base 4bf9603 differ only in the four new plan/script files (git diff --stat: harness_labs/ and tests/ identical), so the base choice itself is sound — but candidates stack (each node's base_commit is the prior node's candidate, harness_labs/plan_graph.py:1159-1170, :1417). CB-06's finding test can therefore fail on base because CB-01 added the 'plan' criterion source, and CB-04's can fail with AttributeError on CB-03's new API; both score 'red-green-proven'. Also, only the finding test files are copied into the base tree (red_green_check.py:69-72), so a finding test importing any helper the node added elsewhere under tests/ fails on base as an ImportError and still counts. The plan makes this a prose rule for workers (PLAN.md:20-23) and assigns the check to the reviewer, but the review-stage executor is read-only with tools Read,Glob,Grep only (harness_labs/claude_task_executor.py:43, run_burden_plan_graph.py:503) — it cannot execute anything against the base tree. Mechanically verified as working: `git archive <sha>` from a linked worktree of a linked worktree (tested), and pytest in the extracted tree imports the BASE harness_labs (tests/__init__.py exists, no conftest/pyproject, `python -m pytest` puts the extracted root first — probe confirmed harness_labs resolved to the extracted tree; no site-packages harness_labs installed).
affects: CB-02..CB-07 red phase; the program's central evidence claim

title: Green regression sets are much narrower than each node's blast radius, and the only backstop is a terminal, non-repairable full-suite run
detail: CB-02 rewrites harness_labs/plan_graph.py with regression tests/test_plan_graph.py only (run_burden_plan_graph.py:124-131), yet 13 test modules exercise plan_graph (test_plan_approval, test_plan_graph_integration, test_plan_graph_recover, test_plan_graph_parallel_contracts, test_plan_graph_observability, test_run_catalog*, dashboard tests). CB-01 rewrites controller_kernel.py with two regression targets while 7 modules use it. Those files are not in allowed_paths, so a node that breaks them cannot even fix them. The only global check is the graph functionality command, and it runs once after CB-07 (harness_labs/plan_graph.py:1255-1272): on failure the graph returns 'failed' via audit.finalize with no repair loop and no escalation artifact, so plan_graph_recover has nothing to act on and all seven nodes' work is stranded on retained branches. Runtime is not the constraint — measured full suite 332 tests in 39s (budget 3600s), test_feature_run 23 tests 5.6s, test_controller_kernel 11 tests 0.04s, test_plan_graph 17 tests 2.6s, and no live/network/skipped-model tests exist in tests/.

title: Gate timeout budgets are inconsistent and a timeout produces a traceback instead of the verdict JSON the repair worker is told to read
detail: Each node declares verification_timeout_seconds=1800 for the whole argv (run_burden_plan_graph.py:276), enforced by subprocess timeout on the single invocation (harness_labs/feature_run.py:1587-1603), while red_green_check applies its own default --timeout=1500 to EACH of the two pytest runs (scripts/dev/red_green_check.py:42, :74-77, :85-89) and the runner never passes --timeout (:254-259) — nominally up to 3000s inside an 1800s ceiling. If either internal pytest hits 1500s, subprocess.TimeoutExpired propagates out of run()/main() uncaught, so the process dies with a traceback and no JSON verdict, breaking the verification-repair instruction 'Read the red/green verdict JSON in that evidence' (run_burden_plan_graph.py:534-541). Measured runtimes make an actual timeout remote, so this is a robustness/consistency defect rather than a likely blocker.

title: The approval receipt pins the host python3 by sha256 AND mtime_ns, so any interpreter reinstall between approve and run voids the program
detail: argv[0] is bare 'python3' (run_burden_plan_graph.py:255), so _executable_evidence resolves it via PATH and records path+sha256+size+mtime_ns (harness_labs/plan_approval.py:449-497). Ran prepare_approval against the committed decomposition: gates pass and pin /Users/kirillzaslavsky/miniconda3/bin/python3.13 with mtime_ns 1764387764701730041. _revalidate_host_executables re-checks every field at issue_receipt and again at PlanApprovalAdmission.validate (harness_labs/plan_approval.py:191, :282, :500-533), so a conda update, a `touch`, or a different PATH ordering at run time raises "host executable identity changed" and the whole program must be re-approved. Also confirmed positively: canonical_plan_graph_payload + validate_plan_graph_plan accept the committed decomposition, decompose() reproduces the committed JSON byte-for-byte, and the automatic_recovery mapping passed to register_plan_graph is exactly the v1 field set AutomaticRecoveryAuthority.from_mapping requires (harness_labs/plan_graph_authority.py:47-62).

title: Re-running an attempt with the same --run-id collides on worktree path and feature branch; node worktrees are never cleaned up
detail: feature_run_id is deterministic: f'{graph_run_id}-{node_id}' (harness_labs/plan_graph.py:1402-1403), driving worktree_path=WORKTREE_ROOT/cb-<feature_run_id> and feature_branch=plan-graph/<feature_run_id> (run_burden_plan_graph.py:656-657). GitWorktreeTransaction.create raises "feature worktree path already exists" (harness_labs/git_transaction.py:132-133) and "feature branch already exists" (:166-168). With candidate_only=True and merge=False the runner leaves each node's worktree and branch in place, so any resume/relaunch under the same run_id fails hard rather than reusing or replacing the prior attempt's work — the same class of dead-end the CB-05 diagnosis describes. Verified as fine: worktree-add-from-a-linked-worktree, git archive from the nested worktree, and `git clone --shared --no-checkout` of the linked worktree followed by checkout of a node branch commit (the functionality-test path, harness_labs/plan_graph.py:2040-2052) all work.
affects: relaunch/resume ergonomics; disk retention under WORKTREE_ROOT
